title: Provider candidates adhere and pass correctness but never reach materiality against the legal-vocabulary baseline at these shapes

evidence.note: 4 turns, adhered, no_qualified_candidate; best candidate +2.6% vs baseline, below the 1.05 materiality ratio
M128/K256/N16, 4 turns, adhered, no_qualified_candidate; best candidate +0.6%
4 turns, 6 evaluated candidates, adhered, no_qualified_candidate; correctness clean across all five input cases (max_abs_error ~1.6e-7)
columns=512 (see F-2026-09-10-002), 4 turns, 8 evaluated candidates, adhered, no_qualified_candidate

observation: Across five completed campaigns on Executor v86 under fixed_baseline_paired_metal_v2 (glm-5.3 via claude-code, high effort, 4 turns, 3M token budget), protocol adherence and correctness were perfect everywhere: every evaluated candidate passed all five validation cases with inputs unchanged and max_abs_error at float rounding scale. Not one candidate reached the 1.05 materiality ratio with 6/10 pair wins; every terminal was no_qualified_candidate at maximum_turns. The fixed baseline, authored inside the same legal vocabulary, is already near the performance ceiling the vocabulary admits at these shapes.
proposed_change: Read this as saturation of within-vocabulary optimization, not as a provider-capability result: prefer capability ticks (vocabulary/lowering coverage such as tile_loops, richer access indices, multi-stage reductions) over expecting provider-side improvement inside the current vocabulary at these shapes. Before the next sweep, freeze one fixed baseline bundle per task so successor revisions report baseline movement separately from candidate headroom.
verification_plan: Standing observation to re-measure each tock: rerun the same five tasks on each successor revision with the frozen baseline bundles and compare the candidate-minus-baseline gap series.
